name: Countervailing duty order: DRAMs from the Republic of Korea (C-580-851; 68 FR 47546)
short_name: 2003 US CVD order on Korean DRAMs (Hynix)
authority: US Department of Commerce, International Trade Administration
requirements: Cash deposits of 44.29% on DRAMs and DRAM modules from Hynix and all other Korean producers except Samsung (de minimis subsidies, excluded), after Commerce found Korean government-directed creditor support to Hynix and the ITC found material injury (4 Aug 2003). Later status (revocation) not verified in this run.

name: US-Japan Semiconductor Arrangement (1986)
authority: Governments of the United States and Japan
requirements: Japan to facilitate foreign market access and prevent dumping in the US and third markets [CLM-0099]; MITI implemented it by cutting output/exports to hit price targets, raising DRAM prices (Irwin p. 11). Third-market provision ended 1988 after a GATT panel; US dumping provision ended with the 1991 renegotiated agreement (Irwin pp. 11-12).
